label: in0-gradsup-probe
_why: THE SUPPLIER POINT, MEASURED (user-ruled 2026-09-19: 'Run it against grad-a'). BALANCE_FRAMEWORK 10.86.7. The graded era-0 penalty of 10.86.6 relieves an industry for what it BUYS, and F145 measured what that misses: STEEL, whose inputs are iron and coal, is the binding constraint of the whole chain - demand 0.97 of vanilla, supply three quarters, 18% of its early prices at the +75% ceiling in the SHIPPED CANON where vanilla never touches it - and no input-keyed rule can reach it. The supplier point reaches it from the other side: w = 1 if any tiered rung STANDING ON THE 1836 MAP consumes the industry's own output good, and the score is additive - effective stage = input-side score + k x w.

_arms.probe-gradsup: in0-stage 1.40 / 1.20 / 1.10 with --in0-supplier 0.5 (mode map). The five industries with a named 1836 consumer are relieved: steel (tooling e2, motor e0), tooling (furniture e1), paper (art academy e0), fertilizer (explosives e0) each x1.400 -> x1.300, and explosives (munition e1) x1.325 -> x1.225. Motor scores 0 (automotive does not exist in 1836) and synthetics scores 0 (dye is RAW by ruling, applied symmetrically).

_delta: ONE FLAG against probe-grada, measured at n=2 in session 20260919_142856: --in0-supplier 0.5. Five industries differ, in `inputs` and `target_be` alone; the other twelve are byte-identical, which makes them the control built into the arm. A 2.2 / B 1.5 / cost anchor x 1.9^era / ai_value 1000x3^era / divisor 0.000125 / the 10.75 defines / the 24-month bar throughout.

_predictions._basis: F144 and F145, both at n=2 on the same span and dump dates. Stated before the runs.
_predictions.steel: THE HEADLINE, and the whole point of the term. grad-a reads steel 18 levels / 10.4 STAFFED at 1837.10 (1.00 and 0.75 of vanilla) with 43% of its price readings at the +75% ceiling. Predict gradsup improves BOTH: staffed 0.80-0.95 of vanilla, ceiling share under 35%. ⚠ Steel's own lift falls only 1.40 -> 1.30, so a large move would be a surprise; a move of 0.05-0.15 in staffed share is what the lever is worth. FAILURE MODE: no improvement at all means the supplier point is not acting on the thing it was built for.
_predictions.the_control_inside_the_arm: food, textile, furniture, glass, arms, artillery, motor, munition, automotive, electrics and the academy have IDENTICAL recipes to grad-a, so their era-0 margins and staffing retention should match grad-a's within seed noise. If they move, the difference is not the supplier point - it is the market, and the read needs a third run.
_predictions.world_product: grad-a 0.99 of the control. Relief can only add, so predict 0.99-1.02. A fall would mean the relieved industries crowd something out.
_predictions.engines: motor's own lift is UNCHANGED at x1.20, but its only input is steel and steel is now cheaper to run, so engine supply should improve: predict consumption above grad-a's 0.62 of vanilla and the ceiling share at or below its 30%.
_predictions.the_relieved_but_healthy: tooling and paper are among the healthiest industries at every in0 tested and take the same -0.10 as steel. Expect no visible change in them - that is the rule spending a little where nothing was wrong, and it is the acknowledged price of a rule over a fit (10.86.7).

_comparison: probe-grada (20260919_142856, n=2) is the paired arm; the flat and vanilla references of 20260919_132049 come in through `early_probe --also`. All three sessions share the machine, day, game version, span and dump dates.

_caveats: TWO IN-GAME YEARS IS NOT THE CENTURY: this measures whether the supplier point moves the anchor's steel, nothing else.
n=2, and the steel LEVEL count is a coarse integer; STAFFED levels is the primary measure (F144 §2a).
The supplier weights are derived from the 1836 map by ruling, so they are an anchor-time number; the late game is deferred, not answered.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent.
